**7B.3 — Research Note**
Bottom line: mixed, leaning no. I found some evidence of technocratic / rule-based economic management, but the broader 2024 record still shows heavy personalization, patronage, and use of state power to protect the ruling coalition’s political interests. I did **not** find a clean 2024 source directly proving family-business self-dealing in a specific contract or license award.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Pakistan IMF reaches agreement on economic policies for 37-month EFF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff) | IMF | 2024-07-12 | Sharif’s government tied policy to diagnosis and correction: broaden the tax base, improve SOE management, strengthen competition, and expand BISP plus health/education spending. This is the strongest evidence for moving state policy away from patronage and toward rules. | IDs: `7B.3`, `6B.10`, `7B.2`
- [Pakistan PM to choose banker Aurangzeb as finance minister, sources say](https://theprint.in/world/pakistan-pm-to-choose-banker-aurangzeb-as-finance-minister-sources-say/1996592/) | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-03-11 | Sharif picked a career banker to run finance instead of a purely political loyalist. That supports a competence-first, less patronage-heavy approach in the economic portfolio. | IDs: `7B.3`, `6B.10`
- [PM forms new economic advisory council without Dar, Aurangzeb](https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/1190715-pm-forms-new-economic-advisory-council-without-dar-aurangzeb) | The News | 2024-05-19 | Sharif created an advisory council of economists, technocrats, and business figures to guide policy. That is evidence of some separation between day-to-day state decisions and narrow political loyalty. | IDs: `7B.3`, `6B.10`
- [PM Shehbaz directs full digitalization of social welfare payments under BISP](https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-directs-full-digitalization-of-social-welfare-payments-under-bisp/) | APP | 2024-03-18 | BISP payments were pushed onto digital wallets to curb leakage, delay, and discretion. That is a concrete anti-patronage delivery reform rather than a loyalty-based cash distribution model. | IDs: `7B.3`, `6B.10`, `6B.8`
- [PM Shehbaz launches 10 mln BISP digital wallets, terms landmark step towards cashless economy](https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-launches-10-mln-bisp-digital-wallets-terms-landmark-step-towards-cashless-economy/) | APP | 2024-08-25 | The government framed the rollout as transparency and financial inclusion. This supports some institutional separation from discretionary favoritism, though it is still executive-led. | IDs: `7B.3`, `6B.10`, `6B.8`
- [Pakistan renegotiating power deals to cut costs, minister says](https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1864298) | Reuters via Dawn | 2024-10-10 | The government renegotiated expensive power contracts to cut tariffs and save about Rs60 billion yearly. That is one of the clearest examples of state action aimed at public cost relief rather than visible private enrichment. | IDs: `7B.3`, `6B.10`
- [PM announces Rs 7.5 billion Ramazan relief package for poor people](https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-announces-rs-7-5-billion-ramazan-relief-package-for-poor-people/) | APP | 2024-03-07 | Relief was presented as a broad anti-inflation package routed through BISP and complaint mechanisms, not a selective loyalty screen. This is a weak but real positive for separating welfare delivery from political patronage. | IDs: `7B.3`, `6B.10`, `6B.8`

**Negative / Counterevidence**
- [Most cabinet choices were still long-time PML-N/PDM hands](https://www.dawn.com/news/1821157) | Dawn | 2024-03-01 | The cabinet still leaned heavily on old political hands, which weakens the case for a clean technocratic break from patronage. | IDs: `7B.3`, `6B.10`
- [Sharif retained direct control over a key economic coordination body](https://www.dawn.com/news/1839967) | Dawn | 2024-06-15 | He kept hands-on control over ECNEC instead of fully delegating to the technocrat finance minister. That suggests personalized executive management still dominated over institutional separation. | IDs: `7B.3`, `6B.10`
- [Pakistan widening crackdown on dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/pakistan-widening-crackdown-dissent) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | HRW said the government clamped down on dissenting media, opposition, and NGOs, creating self-censorship and fear. Using state machinery this way suggests regime-interest protection, not clean separation from political self-interest. | IDs: `7B.3`, `7B.1`, `7B.2`
- [Social media platform X blocked in Pakistan over national security, ministry says](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/social-media-platform-x-blocked-in-pakistan-over-national-security-ministry-says-3382313) | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-04-17 | The state acknowledged blocking X on national-security grounds, restricting criticism and monitoring during a politically sensitive period. That reads as using regulation to protect power. | IDs: `7B.3`, `7B.1`, `7B.2`
- [Pakistan: New Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act threatens the right to protest](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/pakistan-the-new-peaceful-assembly-and-public-order-act-threatens-the-right-to-protest/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-09 | Amnesty said the government rushed through a law that criminalized peaceful assembly and widened restriction powers. That is strong evidence of coercive state use against critics, not separation from political interest. | IDs: `7B.3`, `7B.1`, `7B.2`
- [Pakistan government intensifies crackdown on political dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-09 | HRW reported mass arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, and mobile-internet cuts against peaceful protesters. This is direct evidence of law enforcement being used as a political instrument. | IDs: `7B.3`, `7B.1`, `7B.2`
- [Pakistan’s government curbs judiciary’s power after alleged harassment of MPs](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps) | The Guardian | 2024-10-21 | The 26th Amendment weakened judicial independence amid intimidation allegations. That cuts against using courts as neutral checks on personal or coalition power. | IDs: `7B.3`, `7B.1`, `7B.2`
- [Dangerous digital crackdown](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/12/12/dangerous-digital-crackdown) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-12-12 | HRW said internet throttling, VPN restrictions, and PECA-based controls were expanding by late 2024. That is evidence of state control being used to protect the regime’s informational environment. | IDs: `7B.3`, `7B.1`, `7B.2`
- [Pakistan controversial Punjab Defamation Act signed into law](https://www.loc.gov/item/global-legal-monitor/2024-06-25/pakistan-controversial-punjab-defamation-act-signed-into-law) | Library of Congress | 2024-06-25 / 2024-06-26 | Critics said the act created tribunal and platform-suspension powers that could be weaponized against critics and media. This is strong evidence of regulation being designed in a way that can serve political control. | IDs: `7B.3`, `7B.1`, `7B.2`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a clean 2024 source directly tying Shehbaz Sharif or his immediate family to a specific contract, licensing decision, or procurement award that clearly showed personal/business enrichment.
- The strongest negative evidence is therefore indirect: personalized control, patronage-heavy staffing, and use of law enforcement / regulation / media controls to protect regime interests rather than clearly neutral state separation.
